input_constraints: Read-only source: the ISO is opened for reading and a build writes a NEW image that must not already exist; the source is never touched.

One texture, one PNG, one write. A PNG must be exactly the texture's size and is indexed against the member's own CLUT, keeping the index the file already used wherever a pixel is unchanged; a colour the palette does not hold lands on the nearest one it does and the receipt reports the worst channel error.

Fixed allocation wherever it fits: the rebuilt member is re-packed under the codec that fits the slot it already owns, and the receipt says which codec and how many bytes. A rewrite that would grow the container past its ISO extent is refused rather than relocated.

The preload caches are part of the write. FLDDATA.DAT's directory is copied once into the preload caches and 21 of its members; UIS_TMLO.DAT's directory once and eight of its members. Every copy the edit disturbs is rewritten from the container's own new bytes, and a CARRIED member whose stored size changed is refused by name, because a cached copy is a fixed slot.
It does not create a team: the create-a-school colour and uniform tables are shipped with 0 rows. It does not know which field or which school a member is; neither container names its members.

The verifier imports none of the writer: it re-decodes the texture out of the destination, compares every untouched member byte for byte, re-reads every preload-cache copy off the NEW image, and fails on a byte changed outside the declared ranges.
portme: A runtime witness would be a PCSX2 boot of a rebuilt image showing the replaced texture on screen. Nothing here has been booted.

The PCSX2 texture dump paired with SLUS-21752 is TWO frames of one matchup, so 510 of the 16,308 textures the six art rows reach carry a CONFIRMED replacement name and every other one is DERIVED from the texture's own bytes. Seven of the twelve art containers -- COACFACE.DAT, FANDATA.DAT, LOADDATA.DAT, MSCTDATA.DAT, UIS_GEAR.DAT, UIS_STAD.DAT, UIS_TMLO.DAT -- were drawn by neither frame and have no confirmed name at all. A gear screen, a school-logo menu, a stadium select, a load screen and a mascot or trophy cut-scene would reach all seven; the per-container counts are in docs/product/measured/ncaa09_ps2/pcsx2-texture-identities.json.
Which school, stadium or player a member belongs to is not established: none of these containers names its members, and no table on this disc joins a row to a texture.

gui.reason: Surfaced on the Menus & UI page of the PS2 NCAA 09 Studio as an editor, one target per string slot. Each target carries the room it has -- which on this disc is exactly the length of the string that is there, because no bank ships with padding -- and a replacement that does not fit is refused inline with the number of characters it has to lose. A preview re-reads the strings off the user's own disc on demand; the catalogue document never carries one. input_constraints: Read-only source: the ISO is opened for reading and a build writes a NEW image that must not already exist.

A string slot is a fixed allocation. A shorter replacement is padded to the slot with the format's own terminator, so the string the game reads ends where the replacement ends and every byte after it inside the slot is a NUL; a longer one is refused with the length it has to fit. Because the allocation counts the padding a previous edit left behind, shortening a string does not spend it.

EXAMS.DAT, JERSEY.DAT and OSDKSTRN.DAT are named by NONE of the three QL01 preload caches, which is what makes them safe to write. GAMEDATA.DAT IS named, by FE.QKL and GAME.QKL, and is refused with the sentence naming them: editing one copy and not the other would leave the game reading whichever it reached first. The list is read off the user's own image rather than trusted from a table written down here.

latin-1 and never utf-8: that is the encoding EA stored these banks in, and a character outside it is refused by name rather than mangled. FONTS.DAT and UIS_FONT.DAT hold 17 FNTS font sets and no decoder for that format exists here, so which characters actually have a glyph is not something this row can tell you.

Nothing moves: the member keeps its exact byte count, so the container does, so the ISO extent does, and the destination image is the source's exact size. The verifier imports none of the writer -- it re-reads every edited slot out of the destination, compares every untouched member byte for byte, and fails on a byte changed outside the declared ranges.
The catalogue carries no string. Counts, lengths and digests only; a string reaches a screen through a target or a preview, both read from the user's own image.
portme: A runtime witness would be a PCSX2 boot of a rebuilt image showing the replaced string on the screen that draws it. Nothing here has been booted.
GAMEDATA.DAT's one bank needs the preload-cache rewrite the art and roster rows already do; it is refused here rather than written half.
No FNTS decoder exists in this repository, so a replacement that uses a character the shipped font has no glyph for cannot be caught before it is written.

gui.reason: Surfaced on the Names, Numbers & Faces page of the PS2 NCAA 09 Studio as an editor, one target per player row of the 432 rosters. The controls are the squad number, the position id, the college class, the redshirt flag, height, weight and the twenty attribute fields; the depth chart's three fields are editable beside them. The page must not draw a name field -- there is none on this disc -- and must not draw a 0-99 rating spinner: these fields are FIVE bits and the bound is 31, which is what the editor offers. Budgets and refusals are inline, a dry run resolves every edit before any image exists, and the lane's independent verifier gives the verdict.

input_constraints: Read-only source: the ISO is opened for reading and a build writes a NEW image that must not already exist.

Only LEAGUE.DAT members 1 to 432 are written. Member 0 is the league database and belongs to the Text & Team Identity page's row; GAMEDATA.DAT's 137 databases are the playbooks and belong to the Playbooks & Plays row; TEMPLATE.DAT holds the fresh-dynasty templates; STRMDATA.DB has no PLAY table at all. One page owns one set of bytes.

The ratings are five bits wide, not seven, and the editor's bound is the field's own: 0 to 31. Reading 3,295 records off 62 of the 432 rosters finds every value 0..31 in use with 16% of players sitting on 31, which is the shape of a scale that saturates at its top. What the game DRAWS from those five bits is not established here and no control claims a 0-99 number.

Fixed allocation twice over: a TDB field owns a fixed run of bits in a fixed-stride record, so the database cannot change length, and the member is re-packed under its own RLE1 codec and must fit the slot it already owns. Measured on the retail disc, a PLAY edit in each of members 1, 5, 100 and 432 re-packs to exactly the byte count EA shipped, so the container's directory does not move.

The preload caches are part of the write: LEAGUE.DAT's directory is copied twice and its member 0 once, and every copy an edit disturbs is rewritten from the container's own new bytes. All four CRC-32/MPEG-2 checksum sites are recomputed on every write and re-derived from the destination's own bytes by the verifier, which imports none of the writer.
No row is added or removed, and no PGID is renumbered: a depth-chart slot names a player by the PGID his PLAY row already carries.

It does not edit a kit RECORD, because there is none: CTTB (104 fields), CTCD (45), CTUN (28), USTG, USLG and USLE all have 0 rows on this disc. It does not know which school a member belongs to; the container names nothing and no table joins a TEAM row to a texture.

The verifier imports none of the writer: it re-decodes the texture out of the destination, compares every untouched member byte for byte, re-reads every preload-cache copy off the NEW image, and fails on a byte changed outside the declared ranges.
portme: A runtime witness would be a PCSX2 boot of a rebuilt image showing the replaced texture on screen. Nothing here has been booted.

The PCSX2 texture dump paired with SLUS-21752 is TWO frames of one matchup, so 510 of the 16,308 textures the six art rows reach carry a CONFIRMED replacement name and every other one is DERIVED from the texture's own bytes. Seven of the twelve art containers -- COACFACE.DAT, FANDATA.DAT, LOADDATA.DAT, MSCTDATA.DAT, UIS_GEAR.DAT, UIS_STAD.DAT, UIS_TMLO.DAT -- were drawn by neither frame and have no confirmed name at all. A gear screen, a school-logo menu, a stadium select, a load screen and a mascot or trophy cut-scene would reach all seven; the per-container counts are in docs/product/measured/ncaa09_ps2/pcsx2-texture-identities.json.
Which school, stadium or player a member belongs to is not established: none of these containers names its members, and no table on this disc joins a row to a texture.

runtime.scope: Offline only. Every step is proved against the user's own bytes -- the member decodes back to the pixels that were given, the container keeps the layout rules the retail discs follow, every untouched member is byte-identical, every preload-cache copy still equals what it copies, and the image-level verifier re-derives every declared byte from the two files -- and NO rebuilt NCAA Football 09 container has ever been booted in an emulator or on hardware. That the game loads the result is not claimed anywhere.
